text: Polygon Labs Member Proposes Hard Fork to Recover Approximately 70.49 Million POL Stolen from Polymarket and Binance A member of the Polygon Labs Validator Support Team has published a Polygon Improvement Proposal (PIP) suggesting a hard fork on the Polygon PoS mainnet to recover approximately 70.49 million POL stolen in two recent hacks involving Polymarket and Binance, valued at about $6.5 million based on October 29 prices. Of the total, Polymarket accounts for approximately 23.86 million POL, while Binance accounts for approximately 46.63 million POL. The related funds are currently restricted from transfer by block-producing nodes. The proposal aims to move the POL balances from the attackers' addresses to recovery addresses designated and verified by the two institutions through a hard fork, without changing the total token supply. The proposal will be submitted for discussion at the Polygon Protocol Governance Call on November 5. If approved, client development and testnet rehearsals are expected to be completed in approximately two weeks. — link

text: White & Black Swans If you asked yourself where would BTC trade if Binance was hacked for $6 billion, I think consensus would be around -10% on the day. The only worse scenarios is Saylor or Blackrock being hacked. Even then Blackrock only holds around 70-80 billion vs Binances 140 billion, so we're up there with one of the worst possible hacks/events in crypto's history. Yet we were still only down -3% on the day. On the contrary you have ICE investing in Trade XYZ and Stanley Druckenmiller making his first tweet about being an investor in Hype (arguably the greatest trader of all time). I find it funny that many are calling for Hype to be a short/mid term local top off these news pieces with the rational of "who is bigger than these two news statements?". Yes when looking at price to earnings and other metrics, it would normally be considered overvalued. However in the sense that CEXs are proving to be less and less valuable, stablecoins, privacy and leverage being the dominate metas of the past 12 months, revenue and reflexivity going 100% back to holders, it's tough to call a local top on what can be the asset for the next half decade. The product is the token and the token is the product. Hype, VVV and Zec are the same trade if you're looking for the privacy utility angle post Dem's mid term win. Like I said in previous posts, I don't see mid terms making a difference to markets and we've seen that over the past 24 hours. All things considered, other than war in the Middle East, I'm not overly aware of what other macro negative forecasts there could be. The general thesis I'm seeing is long AI, short AI companies. Betting on the acceleration of models with a mix of frontier usage - top echelons and mega rich paying to use premium services vs bottom k shape using cheaper open source models for mundane tasks. I think this continues to be the trend as corporate tech are too fearful of being priced out of their rat race while the everyday coder doesn't need access to the latest model to complete their passion project. Which essentially leads to larger distribution across AI companies and the leading ones like Claude and Chatgpt slowly lose dominance like Btc/majors do in alt szn. As when everyone is bullish on a trend or usage of products, they realise they get more bang for buck and go down the risk curve. Once AI has its prolonged winter and usage drops off overall with many individuals not being as interested, then I think consolidation goes back into the leading frontier models as it will only be the hardcore power users wanting the best outputs. As we've seen with more experienced devs, most use a hybrid approach where they'll use frontier models to map out product specs and requirements while using open source to complete the low level work for significantly cheaper. I'm still of the opinion that crypto eventually trends up considering how well PA has held given all the negative scenarios. At the same time these bear market chop ranges are enough to drive anyone insane, so I'm not going to keep attempting to call bottoms, although I'll remain optimistic and my outlook is time not priced based. If onchain volume drops another 20-40%, then it'll be on par with the worst conditions we saw throughout 2026. With how much progress we've made in real products and revenue coming onchain, I don't see sentiment being around these levels for too much longer. At the same time there needs to be something exciting and refreshing to respark interest. The launchpad wars thus far have shown little innovation from major players. We're entering the environment where a new player/meta can come along and easily steal mindshare and volume as we're in peak boredom, willingness to experiment is increased due to leaders being stale.

text: Hong Kong Passes Crypto Tax Reporting Law, With Data Collection Starting in 2027 Hong Kong's Legislative Council passed the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and Amended Common Reporting Standard) Bill 2026 on November 4, implementing the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Under the new law, relevant crypto-asset service providers will be required to collect transaction information starting in 2027, with Hong Kong beginning automatic exchanges of crypto-related tax information with partner jurisdictions in 2028. The amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) will take effect in 2028, with automatic exchanges of financial account information under the updated standard beginning in 2029. Hong Kong's Financial Services and the Treasury Secretary Christopher Hui said the legislation aims to strengthen international tax transparency and combat cross-border tax evasion. — link
